mainTopic: A series of cases about a בעל חוב who seizes sold land, orphans paying their father's debt, and a seller's אחריות
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier argument: when an estate was small and then grew, the יורשין already acquired their rights at the time of death. The גמרא then gives a סימן, a memory aid for a list of cases. In the first case, a debtor sold two mansions, and his בעל חוב seized one and came for the other. The buyer offered him the full debt amount. רמי בר חמא compares this to the orphans in our משנה, but רבא answers that the creditor loses nothing. The טירפא document is written for the 500 the buyer actually paid. The same pattern repeats with two small plots of land: רב יוסף compares, אביי rejects, and the הלכה is fifty. Next, אביי rules that when orphans pay part of their father's debt, the creditor may seize the land again, unless they said the money was for the land. Finally, a son who sold his mother's כתובה rights cannot cancel the sale himself, and רמי בר חמא begins a case about ראובן and שמעון and אחריות that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The heirs acquired their rights at the time of death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its comparison: when the estate was small and later grew, the יורשין already acquired their rights at the time of death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as there the heirs acquired rights to them at the time of death, so too when the property was small and then grew, the heirs acquired rights to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an argument that began before this section. It concludes that in a case of נכסים מועטין ונתרבו (property that was small and then grew), the יורשין keep the rights they gained at the time of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is the size of the estate at the moment of death. Growth that happens later does not change how the rights were set at that moment. That is why the heirs' rights stay as they were.

keyTerms.meaning: Were few and then increased (property that grew in value)

steps.whatToRemember: In a case of נכסים מועטין ונתרבו, we look at the estate at the time of death. That is when the יורשין acquired their rights.

phrases.english: the heirs acquired rights to them
phrases.notes: This finishes a comparison from before this section: in the earlier case the heirs gained their rights at the moment of death.

phrases.english: so too, where the properties were few and then increased,
the heirs have acquired rights to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּךְ מוּעָטִין וְנִתְרַבּוּ זָכוּ בָּהֶן יוֹרְשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison from the previous section of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When property was small and then grew, the heirs' rights are fixed by the estate's size at the time of death.

steps.title: A memory aid for the cases that follow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a string of key words, to help remember the order of the coming cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: One thousand, and one hundred, מצוה, in the marriage contract, יעקב, set up, his fields, with words, disputants.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא lists key words to help us remember the cases that are about to come, in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one upcoming case. For example, 'one thousand' points to the case right after this, about a debt of 1,000 זוזים. The list has no ruling of its own. It is just a tool for remembering the order.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid: key words that hint at a list of cases

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to read the סימן as a sentence. It is just a list of hint words, one for each case that follows.

phrases.english: (A memory aid: one thousand, and one hundred,
phrases.notes: 'One thousand' hints at the very next case, about a debt of 1,000 זוז.

phrases.english: מצוה, in the marriage contract, Yaakov,
set up, his fields,
with words, disputants.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A transition. It closes the previous topic and opens a list of related cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This is only a memory aid for the coming cases.

steps.title: A creditor seizes a sold mansion and comes for the second
steps.stepSummary: A man owed 1,000 זוזים and sold two mansions for 500 each. The בעל חוב seized one mansion from the buyer and then came to seize the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man owed one thousand זוזים. He had two mansions and sold them, one for five hundred and one for five hundred. The creditor came and seized one of them, and then came back to seize the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the facts of a real case. A creditor is collecting a 1,000-זוז debt by taking mansions the debtor had already sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two mansions together were sold for exactly the amount of the debt, 1,000 זוזים. The creditor took one mansion, worth 500 at the sale, and now wants the second to cover the rest. This sets up the buyer's response in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They had a claim against him (he owed them)
Seized property from a buyer to collect a debt

steps.confusionAlert: Why can the creditor take a house the debtor already sold? Because the debtor's land is held as security for his debt (שעבוד נכסים). So the creditor can collect from land that was sold after the loan.

phrases.english: There was a certain man
who owed one thousand zuz,
he had two mansions,
he sold them, one for five hundred
and one for five hundred.
The creditor came
and seized one of them,
then he came back to seize the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּהֲווֹ מַסְּקִי בֵּיהּ אַלְפָּא זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first case hinted at by the סימן ('one thousand').
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. These are the facts of the case.

steps.title: The buyer offers the creditor two choices
steps.stepSummary: The buyer goes to the בעל חוב with 1,000 זוזים. He says: either take the mansion you seized as full payment, or take the 1,000 זוזים and give up both mansions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The buyer took one thousand זוזים and went to him. He said to him: If the mansion is worth one thousand זוזים to you, fine. If not, take one thousand זוזים and step away.
steps.whatsHappening: The buyer answers the creditor with an offer that gives him two choices. This sets up the ruling on whether the buyer's claim is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer will not let the creditor take one mansion now and the other later. Option one: the seized mansion counts as payment of the whole 1,000. Option two: the creditor takes the full 1,000 in cash and gives up both mansions. Either way the creditor gets the 1,000 he is owed, and the buyer limits what he can lose.

keyTerms.meaning: Step away, give up your claim

phrases.english: He took one thousand zuz
phrases.notes: 'He' is the buyer of the mansions, not the debtor.

phrases.english: and went to him,
He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִי שַׁוְיָא לָךְ אַלְפָּא זוּזֵי — לְחַיֵּי,
phrases.english: If it is worth one thousand zuz to you, fine,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the first mansion he already seized. Take it as payment for the whole debt.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — שְׁקֹיל אַלְפָּא זוּזֵי וְאִיסְתַּלַּק.
phrases.english: and if not, take one thousand zuz and step away.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁקַל אַלְפָּא זוּזֵי וְקָא אָזֵיל לְגַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the case with the buyer's response to the creditor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. The buyer's two-option offer sets up the question of whether his claim is valid.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא compares the case to the orphans in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא thinks the buyer's offer is like the משנה's case of orphans who offer to raise the value of their father's property by a דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא thought to say: this is the same as our משנה, where the orphans say, "We will raise the value of our father's property by a דינר."
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא tries to decide the mansion case by comparing it to a case in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, orphans offer to value the property higher than it is really worth, and the court does not listen to them. The buyer is doing something similar: he wants the seized mansion, worth 500, counted as full payment of 1,000. So רמי בר חמא suggests the buyer should not be listened to either.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say. This hints that the idea will later be rejected.

steps.confusionAlert: The words סבר למימר warn you that this suggestion will not stand. The very next step rejects it.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama thought to say:
This is the same as our Mishnah:
phrases.notes: The משנה on this daf, where a man left two wives' כתובות and the orphans are dividing the property.

phrases.english: If the orphans said,

phrases.aramaic: ״הֲרֵי אָנוּ מַעֲלִין עַל נִכְסֵי אָבִינוּ יָפֶה דִּינָר״.
phrases.english: "We hereby raise the value of our father's property by a dinar."

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְמֵימַר: הַיְינוּ מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to decide the buyer's offer from step 4 by comparing it to the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the buyer can make the בעל חוב accept the mansion as worth 1,000
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about orphans offering to raise the value of their father's property by a דינר

steps.title: רבא shows the two cases are different
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the comparison. In the משנה the other orphans lose money, but here the בעל חוב loses nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Are the cases alike? There, the orphans suffer a loss. Here, does he suffer any loss? He gave 1,000 and he takes 1,000!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רמי בר חמא's comparison and shows why it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court ignored the orphans' offer in the משנה only because raising the value would cause a loss to the other orphans. The בעל חוב lent 1,000 and is offered 1,000 in full, so he loses nothing. Without a loss, there is no reason to refuse the buyer's offer.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they alike? A standard way to reject a comparison.
There, meaning the case in the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the court's rule in the משנה is about protecting someone from a loss, not a general ban on raising a property's value.

phrases.english: Rava said to him: Are they comparable?
There, the orphans have a loss;
phrases.notes: He means the other orphans, the ones whose mother's כתובה was smaller.

phrases.english: Here, does he have any loss?
He gave a thousand and he takes a thousand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole comparison between the mansion case and the orphans in the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the משנה someone suffers a loss. In the mansion case the בעל חוב suffers none, since he gets back exactly what he lent.

steps.title: How much is the buyer's seizure document written for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what amount goes into the buyer's טירפא document against the seller: 500 or 1,000.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the טירפא document: for how much do we write it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question that follows from the case, and sets up a מחלוקת in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the בעל חוב keeps the first mansion as full payment. The buyer now gets a טירפא, a document that lets him collect back from the seller. He paid only 500 for that mansion, but its seizure wiped out the seller's whole debt of 1,000. So which number goes in the document?

keyTerms.meaning: A document of seizure. It lets the buyer whose land was taken collect back from the seller.

phrases.english: And the seizure document, for how much do we write it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether the buyer's offer works to what happens afterward between the buyer and the seller.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the buyer's claim against the seller is the 500 he paid or the 1,000 debt that was cleared

steps.title: רבינא says 1,000, רב עוירא says 500
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the document is written for 1,000. רב עוירא says it is written for 500.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: for 1,000. רב עוירא said: for 500.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא looks at the result: the mansion paid off the seller's full 1,000 debt, so the buyer can claim 1,000. רב עוירא looks at what the buyer actually paid, which was 500. In his view the בעל חוב's choice to count the mansion as 1,000 does not make the house worth more.

phrases.english: Ravina said: For a thousand.
Rav Avira said: For five hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 7 with two opinions.

steps.title: The הלכה is five hundred
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רב עוירא: the טירפא is written for 500.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: for 500.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the מחלוקת and gives the final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer may claim back from the seller only the 500 he actually paid for the seized mansion. The extra value came from the בעל חוב's own decision, not from the house itself.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is. This gives the final practical ruling.

steps.whatToRemember: The buyer can make the בעל חוב choose: count the seized mansion as full payment, or take 1,000 in cash and give up both mansions. He cannot refuse both, because he loses nothing. But when the buyer then collects from the seller, he gets only the 500 he paid.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: For five hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the מחלוקת from step 8 in favor of רב עוירא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The טירפא is written for 500, the amount the buyer actually paid.

steps.title: A new story: a debtor sells two small plots
steps.stepSummary: A man owed one hundred זוזי and sold his two small plots of land for fifty each. The בעל חוב seized one plot and then came back to seize the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who owed one hundred זוזי. He had two small plots of land and sold them to one person, fifty for each. The creditor came and took one plot, then came back to take the other one too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story that looks a lot like the earlier one, just with smaller numbers. This step only sets up the facts; the legal question comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The debt is 100 and each plot sold for 50, so the two plots together equal the debt. A בעל חוב can take property that was sold after the loan, which is why he goes after the buyer's land. The creditor has already taken one plot and now wants the second.

keyTerms.meaning: Creditor, the one who is owed money
Seizes property from a buyer to collect a debt
There was a claim against him; he owed money

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this story up with the earlier one. The pattern is the same, but here the numbers are 100 and 50, and the names are different.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּהֲווֹ מַסְּקִי בֵּיהּ מְאָה זוּזֵי.
phrases.english: There was a certain man who owed one hundred zuz.
He had two small plots of land.
He sold them to one person, one for fifty
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The square-bracket words are the corrected wording, which says both plots went to the same buyer.

phrases.english: and the other for fifty.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא בַּעַל חוֹב טַרְפַאּ לְחַד מִינַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: The creditor came and seized one of them,
then he came back and was seizing the other one.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּהֲווֹ מַסְּקִי בֵּיהּ מְאָה זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a parallel story with the same structure as the earlier case, but with smaller numbers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the facts: a debt of 100, two plots sold for 50 each, and the creditor seizes the first plot and then goes after the second.

steps.title: The buyer offers the creditor cash
steps.stepSummary: The buyer brings one hundred זוזי and tells the creditor to either treat the land as full payment or take the cash and walk away.
steps.simpleTranslation: The buyer took one hundred זוזי, went to the creditor, and said: if the land is worth one hundred to you, fine; if not, take one hundred זוזי and leave the land alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The buyer makes an offer to stop the creditor from taking his second plot. This sets up the legal question in the next step: does the creditor have to accept?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer gives the creditor two choices. Either he counts what he has as payment of the whole 100, or he takes 100 in cash and gives up his claim on the land. Either way, the creditor gets his full 100.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'to life'; here it means 'fine, very well'
Step away; remove yourself from the land

phrases.english: He took one hundred zuz and went to him
phrases.notes: The buyer is the one going here, and 'him' is the creditor.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי שָׁוְיָא לָךְ מְאָה זוּזֵי — לְחַיֵּי,
phrases.english: and said to him: If it is worth one hundred zuz to you, very well,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — שְׁקוֹל מְאָה זוּזֵי וְאִיסְתַּלַּק.
phrases.english: and if not, take one hundred zuz and remove yourself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story by adding the buyer's offer, which is what the אמוראים will argue about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The buyer offers the creditor his full 100, either as land or as cash, so that the creditor will give up his claim.

steps.title: רב יוסף compares the case to the orphans' משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף thinks this case is the same as the משנה where orphans offer to raise the value of their father's property, and there we do not listen to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף wanted to say: this is the same as our משנה, which says 'if the orphans say...' and the rest of that case.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings the משנה of the orphans as a source for how to rule on the buyer's offer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, orphans offer to value their father's land higher, and the court ignores them. רב יוסף sees the buyer's offer as the same kind of request. If that is right, the creditor would not have to accept the offer.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say; an idea the גמרא may later reject

steps.confusionAlert: 'סבר למימר' is a signal that this idea will probably be rejected. That is exactly what happens in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef thought to say:
This is the same as our mishna:
'If the orphans say,' and so on.
phrases.notes: 'And so on' points to the rest of the משנה case: orphans offering to value their father's property a דינר higher.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר רַב יוֹסֵף לְמֵימַר: הַיְינוּ מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to decide the buyer's offer by comparing it to a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the creditor must accept the buyer's offer of 100.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of orphans who offer to raise the value of their father's property, which the court does not accept.

steps.title: אביי shows the two cases are different
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the comparison. In the משנה the orphans would lose money, but here the creditor lent 100 and gets back 100, so he loses nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Are these cases alike? There, the orphans have a loss. Here, what loss does he have? He gave one hundred and he takes one hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's comparison and shows why it does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason the court ignores the orphans in the משנה is that someone would lose money. Here the creditor gets back exactly what he lent, so there is no loss. Without that reason, the משנה does not apply, and the buyer's offer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they alike? A phrase used to reject a comparison

steps.whatToRemember: A creditor who gets his full money back has no loss, so he cannot refuse the buyer's cash offer.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that the ruling in the משנה depends on someone losing money. Where nobody loses, the comparison falls apart.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Are they comparable?
There, the orphans have a loss;
phrases.notes: He means the other orphans, who would get less when the property is valued too high.

phrases.english: here, what loss does he have?
He gave one hundred, he takes one hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's proof from the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole comparison between the buyer's offer and the orphans in the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's ruling is based on a loss to the other orphans. Here the creditor suffers no loss at all.

steps.title: What amount goes in the טירפא document?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for how much the buyer's טירפא document against the seller is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the document for seizing property, for how much do we write it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about this story. This line sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer lost out because of the seller's debt, so he gets a טירפא document to collect from the seller. The question is which amount that document should state.

keyTerms.meaning: A court document allowing someone to seize property to recover what he lost

phrases.english: And the document of seizure, for how much do we write it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the creditor's rights to the buyer's claim against the seller.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount written in the buyer's טירפא document against the seller.

steps.title: רבינא says 100, רב עוירא says 50
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the document is written for one hundred. רב עוירא says it is written for fifty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: for one hundred. רב עוירא said: for fifty.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different answers to the question about the טירפא document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא writes the full 100. רב עוירא writes only 50, which is the price of one plot. The text gives only the numbers and does not explain either view.

keyTerms.meaning: The Amora who says to write one hundred
The Amora who says to write fifty

phrases.english: Ravina said: For one hundred.
Rav Avira said: For fifty.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: בִּמְאָה, רַב עַוִּירָא אָמַר: בְּחַמְשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the טירפא with two opinions.

steps.title: The הלכה: written for fifty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רב עוירא: the טירפא is written for fifty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: for fifty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument and ends the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling follows רב עוירא, the smaller amount. This matches the ruling in the earlier story, where the הלכה was also the half amount.
steps.whatToRemember: In both stories the ruling is the same: the creditor cannot refuse full payment, and the טירפא is written for the smaller amount.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: for fifty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between רבינא and רב עוירא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב עוירא: the buyer's טירפא is written for fifty.

steps.title: The creditor seizes the land twice
steps.stepSummary: A man died owing 100 זוזים and left land worth 50. The creditor seized it, the orphans paid 50, and the creditor seized it again.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who owed 100 זוזים. He died and left a small piece of land worth 50 זוזים. The creditor came and seized the land. The orphans went and gave him 50 זוזים. Then he seized the land again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story to set up a question about a creditor who takes land, gets paid, and then takes it again. The ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The debt is 100 but the land is only worth 50. When the orphans paid 50, it is unclear what they paid for: part of the debt, or the land itself. The creditor treats it as part of the debt, so he says the remaining 50 still lets him take the land.

keyTerms.meaning: They had a claim against him; he owed them money
Seizes or repossesses property to collect a debt

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּהֲווֹ מַסְּקִי בֵּיהּ מְאָה זוּזֵי.
phrases.english: There was a certain man who owed one hundred zuz.
He died and left a small piece of land
that was worth fifty zuz.
The creditor came and seized it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזוּל יַתְמֵי יְהַבוּ לֵיהּ חַמְשִׁין זוּזֵי,
phrases.english: The orphans went and gave him fifty zuz.
He went back and seized it again.
phrases.notes: He was still owed another fifty, so he took the land a second time.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּהֲווֹ מַסְּקִי בֵּיהּ מְאָה זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case after the ruling on the טירפא document in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the facts: debt of 100, land worth 50, orphans pay 50, creditor seizes again.

steps.title: אביי rules the second seizure is valid
steps.stepSummary: אביי says orphans have a מצוה to pay their father's debt, so their 50 paid part of the debt. The creditor may still seize the land for the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before אביי. He said to them: It is a מצוה for orphans to pay their father's debt. The first fifty you gave was you doing a מצוה. Now, when he seizes the land, he is seizing it lawfully.
steps.whatsHappening: The orphans complain to אביי, and he rules against them: the creditor's second seizure is legal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי treats the orphans' 50 as payment toward their father's debt, which they have a מצוה to pay. That leaves 50 still owed, and the land is still tied to the debt. So the creditor may take the land again.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, the אמורא who gives the ruling
It is a מצוה for the orphans

phrases.english: They came before Abaye.
He said to them:
It is a מצוה for the orphans
to pay their father's debt.
With those first ones, you did a מצוה.
phrases.notes: 'Those first ones' means the first fifty זוזים the orphans paid.

phrases.english: Now, when he seizes the land,
he is seizing it lawfully.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the case described in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The orphans' payment counts as paying part of their father's debt, so the creditor may seize the land again for the rest.

steps.title: A limit: if the orphans said the money was for the land
steps.stepSummary: אביי's ruling holds only if the orphans did not say the 50 was payment for the land. If they did say it, the creditor loses his claim to the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when they did not tell him, 'These fifty זוזים are payment for the small piece of land.' But if they told him, 'These fifty זוזים are payment for the small piece of land,' they have removed him from it completely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits אביי's ruling to the case where the orphans said nothing about what the money was for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on what the orphans said when they paid. If they said nothing, the money goes toward the general debt. If they said it was to buy back the land, the creditor accepted it on those terms and can no longer take the land.

keyTerms.meaning: And we only said this ruling (in a specific case)
The payment or price of something

steps.whatToRemember: When orphans pay a creditor who seized land, the result depends on their words. With no explanation, the money pays part of the father's debt and the creditor can seize again. If they said 'this is for the land,' the land is free.
steps.confusionAlert: The two quotes in the text look almost the same. The difference is not in the wording. The point is whether the orphans actually said these words or not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a practical rule: when paying a creditor, stating clearly what the payment is for can change the legal result.

phrases.english: And we only said this
where they did not say to him:
"These fifty zuz
are payment for the small piece of land."
But if they said to him:
"These fifty zuz
are payment for the small piece of land,"
they have removed him completely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits אביי's ruling from step 18 to cases where the orphans did not say the money was for the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the orphans said the money was payment for the land, the creditor can no longer seize it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The creditor may seize again only if the orphans did not say the payment was for the land.

steps.title: A son sells his mother's כתובה with a condition
steps.stepSummary: A new story: a man sold his rights to his mother's כתובה for a small benefit, and told the buyer he would not repay him if his mother objected.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who sold his mother's כתובה for a small benefit. He told the buyer: If my mother comes and objects, I will not repay you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new case and lays out its facts. The question and ruling about this case come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son had no money yet, only a chance of inheriting his mother's כתובה someday. He sold that chance for a smaller sum. He also told the buyer ahead of time that if his mother objected, he would not pay the buyer back.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract; the money a wife collects if widowed or divorced
A small benefit; a small sum paid for an uncertain right

phrases.english: There was a certain man who sold
his mother's ketubah
for a small benefit.
phrases.notes: He sold his chance of inheriting the כתובה someday, so the buyer paid only a small amount.

phrases.english: And he said to him:
If my mother comes and objects,
I will not repay you.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּזַבְּנַהּ לִכְתוּבְּתַהּ דְּאִימֵּיהּ בְּטוֹבַת הֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the orphans' case and opens a new, separate story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the facts: a son sold his future rights to his mother's כתובה and said he would not repay the buyer if his mother objected.

steps.title: The mother dies silent and the son objects
steps.stepSummary: The story goes on: the mother died without objecting to the sale, and now the son himself comes to contest it.
steps.simpleTranslation: His mother died without objecting, and then he himself came and contested the sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes telling the facts of the story from Step 20. This sets up the legal question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son had only warned the buyer that he would not repay him if his mother objected. She never did object, so that warning never came into play. Now the seller himself wants to undo his own sale, and the question is whether he is allowed to.

keyTerms.meaning: To object to or contest a sale or a claim

phrases.english: His mother died and did not object,
phrases.notes: Some versions read the word with the letters in round brackets and some read it without them. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: and he came and was contesting the sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the facts of the story begun in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case facts: the mother died without objecting, and the son who sold her כתובה rights now contests the sale himself.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא thinks the son stands in his mother's place
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא first suggests that the son inherits his mother's right to object, so his objection works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא thought to say: he stands in his mother's place.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא offers a first idea: the son takes over his mother's position, so he can object just as she could have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother could have objected to the sale. Now that she has died, the son is her heir, so רמי בר חמא reasons that her right to object passes to him. The word סבר tells us this is only a first thought, and it is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say. This marks a first idea that is usually rejected afterward.
He stands in his mother's place, as her heir

steps.confusionAlert: Do not take this as the final ruling. סבר למימר signals a proposal that רבא rejects in the next step.

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama thought to say:
he stands in his mother's place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to whether the son's objection counts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First idea: as his mother's heir, the son takes over her right to object, so he may cancel the sale.

steps.title: רבא: the son guaranteed against his own objection
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רמי בר חמא's idea. The son only refused to guarantee against his mother's objection. He certainly guaranteed that he himself would not undo the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: granted that he did not take on a guarantee against her objection, but did he not take on a guarantee against his own?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רמי בר חמא with a question that really means 'Of course he did!' The son cannot undo his own sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son's warning only freed him from responsibility if his mother objected. It did not free him from responsibility for his own actions, because every seller promises not to cancel his own sale. So even though he is her heir, his objection is blocked by his own אחריות.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantee or responsibility a seller takes on toward the buyer
Granted, even if we accept that...

steps.whatToRemember: A seller who refused responsibility for someone else's claim is still responsible for his own. He cannot later cancel his own sale, even after inheriting that other person's rights.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the idea that a seller is always committed against his own claims, and רמי בר חמא's next case builds on this kind of reasoning about אחריות.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Granted that a guarantee against her
he did not take upon himself,
a guarantee against himself, did he not take on?
phrases.notes: This question really means 'Of course he did!' Every seller promises he won't take back his own sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא נְהִי דְּאַחְרָיוּת דִּידַהּ לָא קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רמי בר חמא's proposal from Step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the son's objection is valid because he inherits his mother's place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores that the son, as the seller, personally guaranteed against any objection of his own, and that guarantee still binds him as her heir.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The son cannot cancel the sale of his mother's כתובה rights.

steps.title: New case: a field sold without a guarantee, then sold back with one
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא begins a new case. ראובן sells a field to שמעון without אחריות, and then שמעון sells it back to ראובן with אחריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: ראובן sold a field to שמעון without a guarantee, and then שמעון sold it back to ראובן with a guarantee.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a related case about guarantees. This step only lays out the facts. The ruling comes after this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sales are not equal. ראובן gave שמעון no guarantee, but שמעון did give ראובן a guarantee. This sets up a question about what happens if the field is taken away, which the גמרא answers next.

keyTerms.meaning: Without a guarantee. The seller will not pay back the buyer if the field is taken away.
Sample names the גמרא uses for two parties, like 'Person A and Person B'

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
If Reuven sold a field to Shimon
without a guarantee,
and Shimon came and sold it back to Reuven with a guarantee,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא רְאוּבֵן שֶׁמָּכַר שָׂדֶה לְשִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁלֹּא בְּאַחְרָיוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, related case about אחריות after רבא's point about the seller's own guarantee.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case facts only: ראובן sells to שמעון without אחריות, and שמעון sells back to ראובן with אחריות. The ruling has not been given yet.
